idea_name: Box-counting information dimension of increments in lag space
mechanism: Immerse quote increments Δc_t into a D-dimensional lag vector; estimate information dimension by box-counting (ε halved in bits) on the point cloud. If empirical dimension ≪ D (e.g. ~4 in a 15-D immersion for S&P500), the series is partly deterministic/chaotic rather than i.i.d.—a binary predictability/structure sensor that rejects efficient-market noise.
data_needed: Long history of quote increments; immersion depth D; box-counting over dyadic ε
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: S&P500 monthly index, 679 values; also discussed for DM/$ daily and Lukoil futures hourly
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS an a-priori structural predictability gauge (dimension gap vs lag depth) before any NN is trained, usable as a regime filter for when sequence models are worth running.
quote: the experimental points form a set of the dimension of approximately 4 in a 15-dimensional immersion space. This is much less than 15 that we would obtain based on the efficient market theory

mechanism: Estimate cross-entropy I(x_{t+1}; past window) of next increment sign given immersion depth via box-counting; plot I vs window width. Rising then falling I identifies an optimal lag horizon (here ~25 for S&P500) beyond which extra history adds noise—sensor of useful memory length for sequence models.
data_needed: Increment series; box-counting cross-entropy over immersion depths
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: S&P500 monthly increments; immersion depths up to ~25+
why_new_for_mis: Turns ‘how much history to feed the sensor’ into an empirical information curve rather than a fixed hyperparameter—MIS can retune lag depth when the I-peak shifts.
quote: Increasing immersion depth over 25 will be accompanied by decreasing predictability.

idea_name: Wavelet-selective-accuracy coding of long price windows
mechanism: Replace raw lag immersion with a wavelet coefficient vector that reconstructs the recent past accurately and the remote past only in outline (highs/lows). Example: 50-point window → 10 wavelet coeffs. Use the compressed vector as NN inputs so horizon expands without exploding input dimension.
data_needed: Price/increment window; wavelet basis; coefficient selection/compression
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Illustrative 50-value reconstruction; applicable to S&P500 and FX series in article
why_new_for_mis: Provides a multi-scale memory sensor that preserves distant extrema psychology without the curse of dimensionality of flat lags.
quote: the immediate past of the time-series is reconstructed accurately, while the remoter past is restored in general outline, highs and lows being reflected correctly. Therefore, it is possible to describe a 50-dimensional window with just 10-dimensional input vector

idea_name: Coterie NN dispersion as forecast-confidence sensor
mechanism: Train L networks on the same sample with different random initial weights; use the mean (or adaptively weighted) coterie vote for the next-step sign, and the dispersion of expert outputs as a live confidence/uncertainty sensor that scales position size δ∝confidence. Uncorrelated experts cut MSE by ~√L.
data_needed: Ensemble of NNs; same feature set (e.g. EMA 1…30 of increments, or Fib-period EMAs); validation for adaptive weights
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: S&P500 last 100 test points; coteries of 10 and 25 nets; also DM/$ daily and Lukoil hourly
why_new_for_mis: Converts ensemble disagreement into an explicit uncertainty sensor for MIS risk gating—not just a better point forecast.
quote: The dispersion of experts' predictions will give an idea of the confidence level of these predictions, which can be used for choosing a correct trading strategy.

idea_name: FX inverse-symmetry hints to augment neural training sets
mechanism: Exploit DM/$ ↔ $/DM inverse symmetry: for each training example of relative increments, add its sign-flipped reciprocal analog, doubling samples and constraining the hypothesis class. Reported ~2× profit rate (5%→10% p.a. after costs) on basic FX.
data_needed: FX quote series; paired examples (x, Δ) and (1/x, −Δ) style transforms
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Basic forex markets (DM/$ cited); daily horizon in Abu-Mostafa reference
why_new_for_mis: A domain-invariant data-augmentation sensor prior for FX pairs that MIS can bake into sequence training without new labels.
quote: for basic forex markets, the consideration of symmetry increases the profit rate nearly twice, specifically: from 5% to 10% per annum considering real transaction costs

idea_name: 30-indicator ternary signal matrix for package selection
mechanism: Each tick/bar write a 30-row digital matrix of flags ∈{−1,0,1} for AC, A/D, Alligator+Fractals, Gator, ADX, ATR, AO, Bears/Bulls, BB, CCI, DeMarker, Envelopes, Force, three Ichimoku rules, MFI, MA, two MACD rules, two OsMA rules, SAR, RSI, RVI, StdDev, two Stochastics, WPR. Classify rows as constantly-significant (never 0) vs pointwise-significant. On a manually marked trend window, keep only indicators whose flags match the trend—forming a consensus package; Main Flag = conjunction of chosen flags for buy/sell tests.
data_needed: Standard MT4 indicator buffers with optimizable periods; chart objects for matrix text; selected trend interval markers
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: generic MT4 symbols/periods; package tested via strategy block on history
why_new_for_mis: Turns indicator soup into a synchronized ternary panel sensor so MIS can score which classical features currently cohere with realized trend regime.
quote: The appearance of "-1" in a certain matrix line denotes the presence of a signal to sell produced by a certain indicator (oscillator); appearance of "1" - presence of a buy signal, "0" denotes the absence of any signal.

idea_name: Clock-hour average bar-height and body-direction market pulse
mechanism: Export OHLC; compute bar height High−Low (and optionally Close−Open); pivot-average by clock Time of day to get mean range and mean signed body per hour. Peaks mark session activity waves (e.g. 08–09 and 14–16); signed bodies mark habitual direction. Classify markets as white-noise / quiet-block / fluctuating / aggressive / two-wave from the pulse chart.
data_needed: History Center CSV; Excel pivot or ft.BarStatLine averaging body, shadow, bull/bear majority, mid-body shift by time-of-day
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: NZDUSD, AUDNZD, EURCHF, USDCAD, USDCHF; H1 primary; also M5/M15/M30 for when regularity appears; monthly vs 3-month windows (e.g. USDCAD Mar 2008 vs Jan–Mar 2008)

idea_name: Analysis-window length where intraday pulse regularity appears then cancels
mechanism: Recompute the same time-of-day averages over short vs long calendar windows. Short windows (≈1 month) show clear directional blocks; longer windows (≈3 months) can wash to neutral noise when early trends reverse—use disappearance of pulse structure as a regime-change/reversal sensor. Also require TF coarse enough (≈M30+) for activity regularity to stand out of noise.
data_needed: Same per-hour aggregates over rolling calendar lengths and TFs
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDCAD H1 Mar 2008 vs Jan–Mar 2008; M5/M15/M30 comparisons
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a meta-sensor on the stability of session structure itself—when the pulse flattens, treat prior session habits as stale.

idea_name: Servo equity attractor and bifurcation around task g
mechanism: Drive dy=dx*(y−g)*m (or |y−g|*m+c) so equity y is attracted to task g. g is an attractor under down/flat and a bifurcation point if the system is not allowed to stick; linear rising g produces follow-up with rare large drawdowns that reverse into a drawdown-limit technique. Sense distance-to-task and side-of-task as continuous control-state features.
data_needed: Price increments dx; tunable m,g,c; multilevel chart transforms before last real level
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: ACS framing; field-proven but instrument-agnostic; mentions multi-pair parallel sync
why_new_for_mis: Reframes MIS state as distance/side relative to an equity attractor rather than only price prediction—useful for always-in-market control sensors.
quote: g is an attractor (a simple one, though there can occur complicated ones, too), i.e., it is a state the system is attracted to by the down-trend or by the flat market. It is also the point of possible bifurcation

mechanism: Two subsystems exchange: dy1=dx*(k1*y1+k2*y2−g)*m, dy2=−dx*(k2*y1+k1*y2−g)*m. Regime map: k1>0.5 converge; k1=k2=0.5 self-oscillation (speed follows g); k1<0.5 diverge with accelerating amplitude about zero. Amplitude ratio >1 is an instability sensor; fake/auxiliary systems can feed real ones.
data_needed: Paired equity states; k1,k2,g,m; optional sine kickstart
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: theoretical ACS examples; >1000 horizontal / >10 vertical systems mentioned in practice
why_new_for_mis: Supplies explicit coupled-system regime labels (converge/oscillate/diverge) MIS can monitor on synthetic sleeves without predicting price direction.
quote: If k1 < 0.5 and k2 > 0.5, then the system diverges. It is still oscillating about zero, but its amplitude increases with acceleration

idea_name: Random ±1 speed transform retaining only volatility path
mechanism: First transform dy=dx*k(i) with k(i)∈{−1,+1} (or continuous [−1,1]) strips directional content so the resulting chart carries mainly volatility (plus some local path properties). Parallel many such charts, synchronize freezes to control spread, then apply higher-level transforms—volatility-only sensing substrate decoupled from crises of direction.
data_needed: Price dx; PRNG for k; multi-system sync rules; optional 1.5h decision grid
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: abstract ACS; modeling horizons up to ~1000 years cited; multi-pair parallel
why_new_for_mis: Builds a direction-agnostic volatility canvas for MIS stress tests and crisis-immune secondary sensors.

idea_name: Wolfe-wave channel with fibo-projected EPA and 2-4 break
mechanism: Mark points 1–5 in a narrowing/parallel channel: fibo between 2–3 projects point 4 into 38–61% retrace and point 5 near 138/161% of 2–3; join 5–3 to locate true point 1 on 1–2, then ray 1–4 projects EPA point 6. Optional fibo time zones. Entry sensor: candles break trendline 2–4; quality prior: equal time spacing of 1–3–5 (symmetry).
data_needed: Swing highs/lows; fibo levels; trendlines 1-3-5 and 2-4; optional time fibo
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any markets/TFs; example formation end-2009; fractality across higher TFs noted
why_new_for_mis: Structured channel-breakout change sensor with explicit geometric target and symmetry quality score—usable as a pattern-regime detector beyond plain S/R.
quote: A confident market entering can be performed after candles break out the trend line that joins points 2 and 4. ... The most precise models are obtained when time intervals between points 1-3-5 are equal.

idea_name: Post-session continuation hit-rate vs session high/low invalidation
mechanism: Label a clock session bullish/bearish/neutral by Open vs Close of the session window; set virtual TP = Close±Profit and SL = session Low (bull) or High (bear); over next Hour_kol_vo hours count TP vs SL hits. Resulting probabilities are a session-to-day continuation sensor; article finds myth weak at 15–25 pts on 50 days, but EURUSD 5-pt TP after 03:00–13:00 hit 100% in that sample.
data_needed: H1 bars; session open/close clock; Day_kol_vo, Hour_kol_vo, Profit; broker STOPLEVEL
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY, EURUSD, GBPJPY, NZDUSD; H1; windows 03:00–13:00, 03:00–09:00, 09:00–13:00; last 50 days; Profit 5/15/25 points

idea_name: S/R-midpoint refhit gated M1 two-candle price-action patterns
mechanism: Mark subjective support, resistance, and midpoint refs. Set refhit when price reaches ref (e.g. O2<ref && C3≥ref). Only then arm three M1 two-candle setups—(1) long-wick reversal past prior high/low, (2) tweezers equal-body opposite closes, (3) second candle closes fully past first—and enter at open of candle 3 if both pattern candles close on the trade side of ref. Tight SL (~10 pts) near structure.
data_needed: M1 OHLC; manually or algorithmically chosen ref levels; pattern boolean gates
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex, stocks, commodities; always M1 for entry; EURUSD examples refs 1.09000, 1.07690 near support 1.07660
why_new_for_mis: Combines level proximity with micro price-action confirmation into a gated change sensor—MIS can treat refhit+pattern as a high-precision local reversal/continuation event stream.
quote: When one of these patterns is seen near a reference price level (support, resistance or midpoint), market entry occurs exactly at the opening price of the next (third) 1-minute candlestick.
